title: Merrill Lynch -  first among peers to fiduciary?
description: Merrill Lynch has taken out a full-page ad in the Wall St. Journal saying it is first among it's peers to support the fiduciary rule and that it does so wholeheartedly. If they hold themselves to fiduciary for non-retirement accounts, then they can say it's real. We'll see.

asr.full_text: Hi, my name is Mike Gary and my company is Yardley wealth management or fee only investment management and financial planning firm and newtown bux County Pennsylvania anybody see the ad full-page ad buy bank of america mary lynch in The Washington Journal today its least wanted me may have been a couple at the back of a section I talked about moving to a fiduciary duty and putting clients front and center and it's really interesting we'll see how they go I think they say that they are a leader among their peers and I'll be interested to see how they actually move you know because the big brokerage firms have been fighting the fiduciary standard for twenty years and trying to say that their broker dealer reps are advisors but not be held to an advisory standard. I think it would be great if they actually do go forward with that. We'll be able to see, we'll be able to tell, because right now that fiduciary standard for them will only apply to retirement accounts and so come next April if they don't apply that for non-retirement accounts and and don't hold themselves set for non-retirement accounts well then then they're just doing what the law requires them and then I don't know if that's really a reason to celebrate in an ad so we'll give them the benefit of doubt I hope that is true it would be a good thing for clients. I think the advisors there or brokers there would be happy with that, would like it and we're going, it's a good standard, it's the right thing. Put your clients interest first, put them front and center, that's perfect. We'll be interested to see. The proof will be in the pudding next year after That is adopted that the Department of Labor's fiduciary standards are adopted for those firms for retirement accounts if They get sued Relating to a brokerage account and they say they're not liable because they're not held to a few You know they shouldn't be held to a fiduciary standard because it's not a fiduciary count? Well, if they still stick with that, then the advertising doesn't really mean anything. Nobody takes out an ad saying, hey, we're complying with the law. So I hope they don't anyway. So it'll be interesting to see. I hope that it is a new step for them and that they're a leader among peers. They have been leaders in the past, lots of times. I hope this is one of those times. I worked there from 1998 to 2001 and most of the time I was a big fan. You know, everybody has some missteps, but we'll see what happens.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents financial-industry commentary about Merrill Lynch's claim of supporting a fiduciary rule and evaluates whether that claim has substantive application beyond retirement accounts. The speaker discusses the firm's advertisement skeptically rather than asking viewers to invest, pay, provide credentials, transfer money, or submit private data. The direct-to-camera office setting is consistent with commentary.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary subject is financial-industry commentary about Merrill Lynch's fiduciary-rule advertisement and the conditional implications of applying that standard to different account types. The source does not present an investment offer, return promise, payment request or participation pathway.

evidence.observation: The source describes a Merrill Lynch advertisement claiming leadership among peers in supporting the fiduciary rule.
